_note: Fictional demonstration data for the CLMA board demo. Vendors, proposals and figures are invented and clearly watermarked. No real vendor-confidential information.

meta.title: 2027 Landscape Maintenance Services
meta.term: Two-year initial term (Jan 1 2027 – Dec 31 2028), with two optional one-year renewals by mutual agreement.

rfp.summary: CLMA seeks proposals from qualified firms for full-service landscape maintenance of the Association's common-area esplanades, medians, right-of-way setbacks, entrances and detention areas. The selected firm will maintain roughly 6 landscaped medians, two monument entrances, a parkway tree corridor and a detention basin to a consistent, board-visible standard.

scope_sections.name: Esplanades & medians
scope_sections.detail: Weekly mowing, edging and litter removal on all median esplanades in season; bi-weekly off-season. Bed maintenance, mulch refresh twice yearly, and weed control.

scope_sections.name: Setbacks & right-of-way
scope_sections.detail: Maintenance of Association-owned setback strips and right-of-way turf to the same standard as the esplanades.

scope_sections.name: Entrance & monument landscaping
scope_sections.detail: Detail maintenance of both entrance monument beds: pruning, fertilization, mulch, and plant replacement within the seasonal-color program.

scope_sections.name: Seasonal color
scope_sections.detail: Rotational annual color at both entrances and designated median nodes. State the number of rotations per year and the plant size/coverage per rotation.

scope_sections.name: Tree maintenance
scope_sections.detail: Structural and clearance pruning of parkway and median trees, deadwood removal, and health monitoring. State the maximum tree height included in base pricing.

scope_sections.name: Irrigation inspection & maintenance
scope_sections.detail: Monthly wet-checks of all zones and controllers, seasonal scheduling, and repair of breaks and controller faults. State what repair scope is included in base pricing versus billed separately.

scope_sections.name: Detention basin
scope_sections.detail: Mowing and vegetation management of the detention basin to district and drainage standards.

performance: Consistent, board-visible standard across all areas; no visibly neglected zones.
Response standard: state the guaranteed response time for routine service requests and for irrigation-main emergencies.
Freeze-event protection of irrigation assets is expected; state inclusion or exclusion.
A named account manager and a single point of contact for the Board.
reporting: Monthly service report with completed-work summary and dated field photos.
Advance notice of seasonal-color rotations and any recommended enhancements.
Irrigation inspection log with any faults found and action taken.
pricing_structure: A fixed monthly base for recurring maintenance, stated as a monthly and an annual figure.
Seasonal color: included in base OR quoted as a separate annual allowance — state which.
Irrigation repairs and tree work: state clearly what is included in base and the unit rates for anything billed separately.
Any board-directed enhancement allowance, if offered.
submission: Company profile, crew capacity and three comparable HOA/district references.
Certificate of insurance (GL, auto, workers' comp) meeting Association minimums.
Itemized pricing on the pricing schedule, signed by an authorized officer.
Statement of any exclusions or assumptions.

proposals.tagline: Incumbent-style base bid — lowest headline price, several services excluded
proposals.response: 48-hour routine response; irrigation emergencies next available crew
proposals.seasonal_color: Excluded from base — quoted as a separate $8,000/yr allowance (4 rotations, pass-through)
proposals.irrigation: Monthly inspection included; all repairs billed time & materials at $85/hr plus parts
proposals.tree_work: Included up to 12 ft; anything above 12 ft billed separately

proposals.tagline: Higher base price, fully inclusive — risk transferred to the vendor
proposals.seasonal_color: Included in base — 4 rotations/yr at both entrances and median nodes
proposals.irrigation: Inspection AND routine repairs up to $1,500 per incident included in base
excluded: Capital replacements above $1,500/incident (billed with board approval)

proposals.tagline: Middle base price — different allowances, CPI escalation, ambiguous terms
proposals.response: "Next business day" for routine service (weekends/holidays undefined)
proposals.irrigation: Inspection included; repairs included up to $750/incident, above that time & materials
proposals.tree_work: Not in base — covered by a separate $6,000/yr tree allowance
proposals.notes: Escalation tied to an unnamed CPI index with no cap; response window undefined for weekends; backflow-certification responsibility not stated.

items: Tree work to a common standard (≤ 20 ft)

normalized.intro: To compare apples-to-apples, each base bid is normalized to a common scope basket: base maintenance + 4 seasonal-color rotations + a routine irrigation-repair budget + tree maintenance to a common ≤20 ft standard. Assumptions are stated so the board can adjust them.
basket_assumptions: Seasonal color: 4 rotations/yr at $2,000/rotation ($8,000/yr) — Proposal A's own quote.
Routine irrigation repairs: $3,000/yr planning budget (from Sterling Ridge irrigation history).
Tree maintenance to a common ≤20 ft standard: $6,000/yr.
normalized.headline_gap_note: On headline base, A appears $27,000/yr below B. Normalized to the same scope basket, A is ~$10,000/yr below B — and B's price already includes irrigation and tall-tree risk plus a 4-hour emergency standard.
normalized.escalation_note: Over the two-year term, A (3% fixed) and B (2.5% fixed) are predictable; C's uncapped CPI escalation is open-ended — at 4% CPI, C's year-two base rises to about $89,200 and a third-year renewal to about $92,800.

amanda.headline: Three responsive proposals. They are not directly comparable as written — the base prices cover different scope, one contains an arithmetic error, and two carry terms that should be clarified before award.

points: Base $6,200/mo. Excludes seasonal color (separate $8,000/yr allowance), irrigation repairs (T&M $85/hr), and tree work above 12 ft.
Base $8,450/mo, all-inclusive: 4 color rotations, irrigation repairs ≤$1,500/incident, tree work ≤20 ft, freeze protection.
Base $7,150/mo. Includes 2 color rotations and irrigation repairs ≤$750/incident; tree work via a separate $6,000/yr allowance.
"Next business day" response. CPI-indexed escalation, no cap.

analysis.title: The apparent low bidder excludes scope the others include
analysis.detail: GreenScape's $74,400 base is the lowest, but seasonal color, irrigation repairs and tall-tree work sit outside it. Normalized to the same scope basket, GreenScape is about $91,400 and the gap to Verdant narrows from ~$27,000 to ~$10,000.

analysis.title: Arithmetic inconsistency in Proposal A
analysis.detail: GreenScape's summary states an annual base of $72,400, but 12 × $6,200 = $74,400 — a $2,000 understatement. The summary figure is unreliable; the corrected base is $74,400.

analysis.title: The bids are not apples-to-apples
analysis.detail: Each base covers different scope (A excludes color/irrigation-repair/tall-tree; B includes them; C is partial). Ranking on headline base misstates true cost — the normalized table is the correct basis.

analysis.title: Escalation terms differ materially
analysis.detail: A is 3% fixed, B is 2.5% fixed, C is CPI-indexed with no cap. Uncapped CPI is open-ended: at 4% CPI, C's third-year base is about $92,800, above its nominal middle ranking.

analysis.title: Allowances are structured differently
analysis.detail: Verdant bundles a $5,000/yr enhancement allowance into base; Lone Star carries a $6,000/yr tree allowance; GreenScape carries none — every extra is billed ad hoc.

analysis.title: Response standards are not equivalent
analysis.detail: Verdant guarantees 24-hour routine and 4-hour irrigation-emergency response; GreenScape is 48-hour; Lone Star is "next business day," which is undefined for weekends and holidays.

analysis.title: Material exclusion in Proposal C
analysis.detail: Lone Star explicitly excludes freeze-event protection of irrigation assets — a real Texas cost and liability the Association would absorb — and does not state who is responsible for backflow certification.

clarifications.question: Confirm the corrected annual base ($74,400) and provide a firm not-to-exceed for the excluded irrigation repairs and tall-tree work.
Confirm the number of seasonal-color rotations and the plant size/coverage per rotation (A quotes a separate allowance; B includes it).
Define "next business day" response for weekends and holidays, and name the CPI index and whether escalation is capped.
Clarify responsibility for freeze-event protection and backflow certification.
Confirm whether the unused $5,000 enhancement allowance rolls over year to year.

amanda.recommendation: This analysis is prepared to inform the Board's decision. It lays out what each proposal says, the material differences, and the questions to resolve. It does not select a vendor — that decision is the Board's.

connected: Vendors, projects, assets and invoices already exist for the operating community (Sterling Ridge). GreenScape Partners currently performs the Median 3 renovation and East Entrance seasonal color; AquaFlow Irrigation performs the Median 7 controller work.
If the Board awards to an existing vendor, its work already flows vendor → project → physical asset → invoice → history, visible in the Operating Map and the Board Report.
conceptual: The RFP document and the three proposals are demonstration artifacts (seeded as real bid_requests / vendor_proposals records, but not solicited from real firms).
The award motion and executed contract are shown conceptually — no binding board vote or contract is created by this demo.
